basis: docs/reviews/2026-11-03-chatgpt-review-of-blog-plan.md — strategy, query, sequencing and standard changes applied

strategy.one_line: Sell the decision, not the catalogue: two commercial lanes, one test lane, and no Profile that the product page already answers.

lanes.why: Established buying job, published prices, two models on the shelf, facilities buyers with budget
Second lane with real institutional demand and a documented purchasing path
High ticket, harder evidence; one comparison to test demand before committing

strategy.mix_note: Mix by publishing effort, not forecast traffic. Re-weight after the pilot on qualified inquiries.

prerequisites.task: Reconcile catalogue price and spec data
prerequisites.detail: 24 models listed on the homepage catalogue, 25 in the plan; Qisheng D2 has a page but no catalogue entry. Published prices exist for Phantas 9,250 / C40-P1 10,700 / MagicDog Y1 64,900 / LimX OLI 65,900 and the plan still said quote-only. One price source feeds catalogue, product page and blog.

prerequisites.task: Attach operating conditions to headline specs
prerequisites.detail: C40-P1 15 h is sweeping; Keenon gives about 5 h for scrubbing. Phantas ~1,180 m2/h is a rate, Gausium's practical efficiency is 350-700 m2/h. MagicDog Y1 carries 150 kg max and 45 kg dynamic payload. No spec ships without its condition.
Model requested, organisation, application, destination, budget state, objection, next action. This replaces guesswork as the priority signal and can override the calendar.
Inquiry form carries the article slug; report qualified inquiries, sales-accepted leads, quotes issued and value. Traffic is diagnostic only.

pilot.continuation_gate: A new Profile is approved only when it has demonstrated sales relevance or a defensible search opportunity, and can add at least three decision-relevant findings the product page does not carry.

inventory.note: The 25-model research inventory is kept — it is where facts and queries live. A model is not a publishing obligation.

models.title_seed: MagicDog: what a 13-DOF quadruped teaches that a simulation cannot
models.angle: The entry legged platform on our shelf. Where the open SDK gets a student to a publishable experiment, and where it runs out of compute.
models.note: deprioritised — casual research traffic, not institutional procurement

models.title_seed: MagicDog Y1: what 45 kg of payload buys on a real patrol route
models.angle: Speed and payload put it in the industrial band. The article sizes a route: sensor bay weight, battery, shift length, and the terrain it still refuses.

models.title_seed: Genisom M1: the 80 cm clearance band, and what it costs to run
models.angle: Clearance is the spec that decides rubble, stairs and site debris. What that buys in field work, and what rugged costs in service and spares.
models.note: delay — needs a real inspection workflow, not rugged-terrain claims

models.title_seed: Keenon C40-P1: how many shifts one charge actually covers
models.angle: 1,100 m2/h and 15 hours on paper. The article turns both into a floor plan, a shift rota and a number the hotel GM can defend.

models.title_seed: Gausium Phantas: four functions, and when the squeegee earns its keep
models.angle: Sweep, scrub, squeegee and dry on one chassis at 1,180 m2/h. Which two functions a hotel actually uses, and what the other two cost to carry.

models.title_seed: LimX OLI: why 157 TOPS decides which research you can run
models.angle: 33 degrees of freedom and Orin-class compute. The article maps the compute budget to real research: perception, whole-body control, or both.

models.title_seed: ADAM U: what USD 45,000 buys in a humanoid lab platform
models.angle: The lowest full-size price on the shelf. What the money covers, what it leaves out, and the first experiment it makes possible.

models.title_seed: ADAM SP: modular actuators and the five-year repair bill
models.query: PNDbotics ADAM SP price and specifications
models.angle: 41 degrees of freedom built on swappable actuators. What repairability is worth over five years, and which failures a lab can fix itself.

models.title_seed: MagicBot G1: general-purpose is a promise — here is the pilot that tests it
models.angle: What a general-purpose humanoid has to prove in 90 days before a plant signs anything, and the three tasks worth starting with.

models.title_seed: AGIBOT X2 Ultra: the half-size humanoid and the venue case
models.angle: At USD 49,999 it lands in venues and retail before factories. What half-size solves, and the interactions it still fumbles.

models.title_seed: AGIBOT A3 Ultra: what a USD 109,999 humanoid must earn each month
models.angle: The top of the shelf. The article works backwards from the price to the hours, the tasks and the payback a buyer has to see.

models.title_seed: Kepler BumbleBee: onboard compute versus a tethered rig
models.angle: 30 degrees of freedom and 100 TOPS in the body. When onboard compute beats a workstation on a cable, and what it costs in battery.

models.title_seed: UniX AI Panther: wheels, 16 hours, and the case against legs indoors
models.angle: 34 degrees of freedom on a wheeled base with a 16-hour battery. Where indoor work rewards wheels, and what a wheeled humanoid cannot reach.

models.title_seed: UniX AI Wanda 2.0: teleoperation as the first deployment
models.angle: Quest 3S control turns a humanoid into a remote worker. What that changes for staffing, and the tasks where latency still shows.

models.title_seed: CASBOT 02 EDU: what students break, and what repairs cost
models.angle: A full-size biped for teaching at USD 69,000. The failure modes a lab actually hits, and the spares a course needs on the shelf.

models.title_seed: AGIBOT D1 EDU: what USD 7,999 includes, and what it does not
models.angle: The cheapest legged platform we list. An honest package list: what arrives, what the course still has to buy, and the labs it can carry.

models.title_seed: Genisom L1: designing a study around a six-kilometre walk
models.angle: A compact research quadruped with a 6 km range. What endurance buys in field studies, and the payload it trades away.

models.title_seed: Genisom L1 EDU: what a curriculum package is actually worth
models.angle: A teaching quadruped shipped with lab modules. When the curriculum saves a term of preparation, and when a lab writes its own anyway.

models.title_seed: CASBOT 4 Piece Band: the economics of a four-robot performance fleet
models.angle: Four coordinated humanoids at USD 333,000. What a venue books, what a show costs to run, and what happens when one robot is down.

models.title_seed: Fourier GR-3: what a 12-DOF hand actually enables in care
models.angle: 55 degrees of freedom, dexterous hands and an emotion engine, built for care. Which care tasks it can hold, and which still need a person.

models.title_seed: DroidUp Moya: the questions to ask before pre-ordering a companion humanoid
models.angle: Announced, not yet shipping. What an unreleased platform has to answer on support, firmware and spares before anyone pays a deposit.

models.title_seed: Xiaoling 3.0: what a USD 5,000 expressive head does in a venue
models.angle: A compact expressive head at USD 5,000. Where it earns its place at a reception or an exhibition, and what it cannot do without a body.

models.title_seed: LDTech Intelligent Head: a USD 6,000 answer to the kiosk
models.angle: Nine degrees of freedom and a voice stack at USD 6,000. When an expressive head beats a screen, and the integration work it needs.

models.title_seed: iSAGE SageMan: four arms against four workstations
models.angle: Plus or minus 0.03 mm repeatability on four arms. When one machine beats four cells, and what the integration still costs.

models.title_seed: Qisheng D2: throughput per square metre in a compact cell
models.query: Qisheng D2 pick and place robot
models.angle: A precision workstation for pick-and-place and inspection. What a compact footprint saves, and where the integration bill lands.
